title: Does Safety Fine-Tuning Become Brittle After Domain-Specific Fine-Tuning?
original_idea: Take a safety-aligned base model. Fine-tune on a domain task (e.g., coding, legal text summarization) with varying intensities (number of examples). Measure safety metric degradation at each intensity level. Identify at what fine-tuning intensity safety becomes meaningfully brittle.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: domain fine-tuning at varying intensity -> safety metric degradation measured -> brittleness threshold identified -> practitioners know when to re-align. Each link is explicit and the deliverable (threshold characterization) has direct practical value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning with standard frameworks (HuggingFace, LoRA) is well-established. Safety benchmarks exist as standard test suites. Methodology is clear: vary examples, measure safety. Intermediate complexity suitable for beginners with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: pick one model, one domain task, vary FT intensity, measure one safety benchmark. The intensity-vs-safety curve is a clear, self-contained result achievable within 30 hours.
